title: Describing and giving opinions
title_target: どうですか — Dō desu ka
goal: Describe things, places and people with adjectives; say what you like and dislike; and give opinions that sound natural, not translated.
bekal: putting adjectives in front of nouns
saying you like something with ～が すきです
giving opinions with とても and あまり

dialogs.title: 会話 1 — How's Tokyo?
dialogs.intro: Tanaka asks Ani about her impressions of Japan. Watch the two kinds of adjectives taking turns — this is the key distinction in this unit.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [とうきょうは|Tōkyō wa] [どうですか|dō desu ka]。
lines.id: How do you like Tokyo?
lines.literal: Tokyo — as-for — how — is — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [とても|Totemo] [おもしろいです|omoshiroi desu]。でも、[すこし|sukoshi] [たかいです|takai desu]。
lines.id: It's really interesting. But a bit expensive.
lines.literal: very — interesting — is. but, a-little — expensive — is.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [そうですね|Sō desu ne]。[へやは|Heya wa] [ひろいですか|hiroi desu ka]。
lines.id: True. Is your room spacious?
lines.literal: so — is — right. room — as-for — spacious — is — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [いいえ|Iie]、[ひろくないです|hirokunai desu]。[せまいですが|Semai desu ga]、[しずかです|shizuka desu]。
lines.id: No, it isn't. It's small, but quiet.
lines.literal: no, spacious-not — is. cramped — is — but, quiet — is.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [しずかな|Shizukana] [へやは|heya wa] [いいですね|ii desu ne]。[ちかくに|Chikaku ni] [なにが|nani ga] [ありますか|arimasu ka]。
lines.id: A quiet room is nice. What's nearby?
lines.literal: quiet — room — as-for — good — is — right. nearby — at — what — [subject] — exists — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [おおきい|Ōkii] [こうえんが|kōen ga] [あります|arimasu]。[とても|Totemo] [きれいです|kirei desu]。
lines.id: There's a big park. It's very pretty.
lines.literal: big — park — [subject] — exists. very — pretty — is.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [にほんの|Nihon no] [たべものは|tabemono wa] [どうですか|dō desu ka]。
lines.id: How about Japanese food?
lines.literal: Japan — 's — food — as-for — how — is — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [おいしいです|Oishii desu]！でも、[なっとうは|nattō wa] [あまり|amari] [すきじゃありません|suki ja arimasen]。
lines.id: Delicious! But I'm not too keen on natto.
lines.literal: delicious — is! but, natto — as-for — not-much — liked — is-not.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [はは|Haha]、[なっとうは|nattō wa] [むずかしいですね|muzukashii desu ne]。
lines.id: Haha, natto is a tough one, isn't it?
lines.literal: haha, natto — as-for — difficult — is — right.

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [でも|Demo]、[すしは|sushi wa] [だいすきです|daisuki desu]。[まいしゅう|Maishū] [たべます|tabemasu]。
lines.id: But I love sushi. I eat it every week.
lines.literal: but, sushi — as-for — big-liked — is. every-week — eat.

notes: **Japanese has two kinds of adjectives**, and they behave differently. **い-adjectives** end in い and change form themselves (たかい → たかくない). **な-adjectives** don't change and lean on です (しずか → しずかじゃありません). Telling them apart is the main job of this unit.

**が in the middle of a sentence means “but”.** せまいです**が**、しずかです = it's small, but quiet. Don't confuse it with が the subject marker — position tells them apart: at the end of a clause it means “but”, after a noun it's the marker.

**きれい ends in い but is not an い-adjective.** This is the most famous trap in Japanese. きれい, ゆうめい and きらい are all **な-adjectives**, despite ending in い. The reason: the い is part of the kanji (綺麗), not an ending. All three must be memorized as exceptions.
**すき isn't a verb but a な-adjective.** すきです = “like”, and the thing liked is marked with **が**, not を: すしが すきです. It feels odd at first, but makes sense once you know すき is closer to “pleasing to me”.
**だいすき = love, really like**; the prefix だい (大) intensifies. Its partners: きらい (dislike), だいきらい (hate).

**あまり + negative adjective** — same as with verbs in Unit 6: あまり すきじゃありません = not very fond of. This is the gentlest way to say you dislike something, and Japanese people use it far more often than きらいです, which sounds harsh.

grammars.title: [い|i]-adjectives — they change themselves
body: [い|i]-adjectives end in **[い|i]** and change their own form to become negative or past. **[です|desu] doesn't change** — it just sits at the end as a politeness marker.
after: **The rule:** drop the [い|i], then add **[くない|kunai]** (negative) or **[かった|katta]** (past).
⚠️ **[いい|ii] (good) is irregular.** Its stem becomes [よ|yo]～: [よくないです|yokunai desu] (not good), [よかったです|yokatta desu] (was good). [いくないです|ikunai desu] is wrong.
⚠️ **Don't write [たかいでした|takai deshita] for the past.** It's the adjective that changes, not [です|desu]. This is the number-one beginner mistake in this unit.

grammars.title: [な|na]-adjectives — they lean on [です|desu]
body: [な|na]-adjectives **don't change at all**. What changes is the [です|desu] after them — exactly like nouns in Unit 1. If you can already change [がくせいです|gakusei desu], you can change every [な|na]-adjective.

head: Form
Example (しずか = quiet)
Meaning
rows: [しずかじゃありません|shizuka ja arimasen]
[しずかじゃありませんでした|shizuka ja arimasen deshita]

after: **Where does the name come from?** From the **[な|na]** that appears when the adjective is attached to a noun: [しずか|shizuka]**[な|na]**[へや|heya]. [い|i]-adjectives don't need it: [たかいほん|takai hon].

**A quick way to tell them apart:** if it doesn't end in [い|i], it's definitely a [な|na]-adjective. If it ends in [い|i], it's almost certainly an [い|i]-adjective — except **[きれい|kirei], [ゆうめい|yūmei], [きらい|kirai]**, three exceptions to memorize.

dialogs.title: 会話 2 — Choosing a restaurant
dialogs.intro: Budi and Ani pick a place to eat. Notice how adjectives are used to compare and give reasons.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [おなかが|Onaka ga] [すきました|sukimashita]。[どこで|Doko de] [たべますか|tabemasu ka]。
lines.id: I'm hungry. Where shall we eat?
lines.literal: stomach — [subject] — became-empty. where — at — eat — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [えきの|Eki no] [ちかくに|chikaku ni] [あたらしい|atarashii] [みせが|mise ga] [あります|arimasu]。
lines.id: There's a new place near the station.
lines.literal: station — 's — nearby — at — new — shop — [subject] — exists.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [どんな|Donna] [みせですか|mise desu ka]。
lines.id: What kind of place?
lines.literal: what-kind-of — shop — is — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [ラーメンやです|Rāmen-ya desu]。[やすくて|Yasukute] [おいしいです|oishii desu]。
lines.id: A ramen shop. Cheap and tasty.
lines.literal: ramen-shop — is. cheap-and — tasty — is.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [いいですね|Ii desu ne]。でも、[こんでいますか|konde imasu ka]。
lines.id: Nice. But is it crowded?
lines.literal: good — is — right. but, crowded-being — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [ひるは|Hiru wa] [とても|totemo] [こんでいます|konde imasu]。でも、[いまは|ima wa] [だいじょうぶです|daijōbu desu]。
lines.id: At lunchtime it's packed. But now it's fine.
lines.literal: midday — as-for — very — crowded-being. but, now — as-for — all-right — is.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [ブディは|Budi wa] [からい|karai] [たべものが|tabemono ga] [すきです|suki desu]。[からい|Karai] [ラーメンは|rāmen wa] [ありますか|arimasu ka]。
lines.id: I like spicy food. Do they have spicy ramen?
lines.literal: Budi — as-for — spicy — food — [subject] — liked — is. spicy — ramen — as-for — exists — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [はい|Hai]、[あります|arimasu]。[でも|Demo]、[すごく|sugoku] [からいですよ|karai desu yo]。
lines.id: Yes, they do. But it's seriously spicy, you know.
lines.literal: yes, exists. but, terribly — spicy — is — you-know.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [だいじょうぶです|Daijōbu desu]。[インドネシアの|Indoneshia no] [りょうりも|ryōri mo] [からいです|karai desu]。
lines.id: No problem. Indonesian food is spicy too.
lines.literal: all-right — is. Indonesia — 's — cuisine — also — spicy — is.

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [そうですね|Sō desu ne]。[じゃあ|Jā]、[いきましょう|ikimashō]。
lines.id: True. Well then, let's go.
lines.literal: so — is — right. well-then, let's-go.

notes: **おなかがすきました = I'm hungry**, literally “my stomach has become empty”. It's past tense although it means now — a fixed expression to learn as is. The opposite: おなかがいっぱいです (I'm full).
**～くて links two い-adjectives**: やすくて おいしい = cheap and tasty. For な-adjectives the link is **で**: しずかで きれい. This connecting form is very common and very economical.
**～や (屋) = a shop selling ～.** ラーメンや (ramen shop), パンや (bakery), はなや (florist), ほんや (bookstore). This one suffix gives you dozens of words.
**こんでいます = is crowded.** The ～ています form expresses an ongoing state; it isn't covered in this module, but the word is too useful to skip.
**すごく = really, super**, a livelier version of とても. A bit more casual, very common in everyday conversation.
**Budi calls himself “ブディは”, not “わたしは”.** Using your own name instead of “I” sounds natural in Japanese, especially in casual talk — something that would sound childish in English.

grammars.title: Saying you like something: ～[が|ga] [すきです|suki desu]
body: The thing liked is marked with **[が|ga]**, not [を|o] — because [すき|suki] is really an adjective, not a verb. The full pattern: **[who] [は|wa] [what] [が|ga] [すきです|suki desu]**.

head: Sentence
Meaning
rows: [わたしは|Watashi wa] [すしが|sushi ga] [すきです|suki desu]。
[わたしは|Watashi wa] [なっとうが|nattō ga] [あまり|amari] [すきじゃありません|suki ja arimasen]。
I'm not too keen on natto.
[アニさんは|Ani-san wa] [おんがくが|ongaku ga] [だいすきです|daisuki desu]。
[なにが|Nani ga] [すきですか|suki desu ka]。
[にほんごが|Nihongo ga] [じょうずですね|jōzu desu ne]。

after: **This [が|ga] family is fairly large:** [すき|suki] (like), [きらい|kirai] (dislike), [じょうず|jōzu] (good at), [へた|heta] (bad at), [わかります|wakarimasu] (understand), [できます|dekimasu] (can), [あります|arimasu]/[います|imasu] (exist). All take [が|ga], and beginners often wrongly use [を|o] with all of them.

⚠️ **Don't praise yourself with [じょうず|jōzu].** When someone says [にほんごがじょうずですね|nihongo ga jōzu desu ne], the natural reply is **[いいえ|iie]、[まだまだです|mada mada desu]** (no, I've still got a long way to go) — modesty is part of Japanese politeness.

grammars.title: Your first forty adjectives
body: The left table is **[い|i]**-adjectives, the right is **[な|na]**-adjectives. Learn them in pairs with their opposites — they stick much faster.
after: ⚠️ The three marked — **[きれい|kirei], [ゆうめい|yūmei], [きらい|kirai]** — end in [い|i] but are **[な|na]**-adjectives. If you memorize only one set of exceptions from this unit, make it these three.

blocks.text: Japanese people rarely state opinions in absolute terms. A softened sentence isn't a sign of doubt — it's a sign of consideration for the listener. The list below runs from most direct to most gentle:

head: Sentence
Meaning
Tone
rows: [ちょっと|Chotto] [からいですね|karai desu ne]。
It's a bit spicy, isn't it?
[あまり|Amari] [すきじゃありません|suki ja arimasen]。
I'm not too keen on it.
[すきじゃありません|Suki ja arimasen]。

blocks.title: Intensifiers and softeners
items: **[とても|totemo]** = very. Neutral, safe anywhere.
**[すごく|sugoku]** = really, super. More casual and lively.
**[ちょっと|chotto] / [すこし|sukoshi]** = a little, a bit. ちょっと is more casual, すこし neater.
**[あまり|amari] + negative** = not very, not much.
**[ぜんぜん|zenzen] + negative** = not at all.
⚠️ とても can't be used with a negative verb. For that, use あまり.

blocks.text: The weather is Japan's number-one conversation opener, and almost all of it uses the adjectives you've just learned.

head: Season
Reading
Typical sentence
rows: [はるは|Haru wa] [あたたかいです|atatakai desu]。 — Spring is warm.
[なつは|Natsu wa] [あついです|atsui desu]。 — Summer is hot.
[あきは|Aki wa] [すずしいです|suzushii desu]。 — Fall is cool.
[ふゆは|Fuyu wa] [さむいです|samui desu]。 — Winter is cold.

blocks.title: Conversation openers that never fail
items: **[きょうは|Kyō wa] [いい|ii] [てんきですね|tenki desu ne]。** — Nice weather today, isn't it?
**[あついですね|Atsui desu ne]。** — Hot, isn't it? (Japanese summers are humid and heavy — you'll use this every day in August.)
**[さむくなりましたね|Samuku narimashita ne]。** — It's gotten cold, hasn't it?
Weather lines work like “how are you?” in English: they don't call for a serious answer, but they open the door.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Japanese. Write in rōmaji.
items: This room isn't spacious.
Tokyo is very interesting.
I like sushi.
I'm not too keen on it.
Nice weather today, isn't it?

answers: たかくないです — おおきくないです — おもしろくないです — じゃありません — じゃありません
が — が — が — は — な — が
ちいさい — ふるい — さむい — せまい — やさしい — やすい
この へや は せまい です — とうきょう は とても にぎやか です — わたし は すし が だいすき です — しずかな へや は いい です ね — この みせ は やすくて おいしい です — なっとう は あまり すき じゃありません

wave: Review Unit 6 through this unit: retell your day, but this time add **one adjective** to each sentence — “every morning I drink hot coffee at a quiet café”. Adjectives are the seasoning that turns a list of activities into a story.
